clue.text: A palace built on a hill, housing a jerk in a leading position?

definitions.text: A palace built on a hill

indicators.note: housing means the next pieces are taken inside the word for the leading position

parts.note: the van is the leading position, as in 'in the van' of an army
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A hilltop palace somehow has a twitching figure installed at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a leading position' echoes the phrase 'in the van', the front of an army. The palace stands on the Vatican Hill in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal residence in Rome stands on the Vatican Hill, one of the city's slopes beside the Tiber.

clue.text: Father Ambrose was one to differ about some scripture

indicators.note: about means the word for differ goes around the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: to differ is to vary
OT, the Old Testament, is part of scripture

explanation.surface: A priest disagreed with others over part of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk such as Scott's Father Ambrose is a devotee, one vowed to religious service.

clue.text: The popular support for the Navy welcomed a ridiculous adventure that killed a pirate

parts.note: popular means in, as in fashion

indicators.note: welcomed means the word for a support takes the escapade inside it

parts.note: a chock is a wedge or fitting that supports a boat or cable on a ship
a caper is a madcap escapade

explanation.surface: Public backing for the fleet embraced a mad venture that did for a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: A chock is a ship's fitting, hence 'for the Navy'. In Southey's ballad, Ralph the Rover removes the warning bell from the reef and later wrecks on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Southey's ballad reef wrecks Ralph the Rover, the sea-robber who had cut away its warning bell.

clue.text: I can be seen in banal work by a French female dramatist

parts.note: corn is trite, banal material

indicators.note: can be seen in means the letter I is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: I appear in a dull piece written by a Frenchwoman playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be seen in' puts I inside ELLE, after its E. Pierre Corneille was the 17th-century French tragedian of Le Cid.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Corneille wrote Le Cid and other classical tragedies for the French stage.

clue.text: Edward, impaled by earl with weapon, was eliminated

indicators.note: impaled by means Edward is pierced, so the other pieces go right into the name

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
a gat is a gun in American slang

explanation.surface: A man called Edward, run through by a nobleman's weapon, was killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impaled by' means the other pieces go inside Edward's short form, just after its first letter; GAT is American gangster slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negated has been nullified or cancelled out of existence.

clue.text: I'm seen in boxes in Austria, according to Shakespeare

indicators.note: seen in means the words I'm are placed within the word for boxes

parts.note: loges are boxes in a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are in theatre boxes, a Shakespearean Austrian among them.
explanation.walkthrough: In King John the Duke of Austria is also called Limoges; the town is also known for its enamelled and porcelain boxes, a nice echo of 'boxes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King John names its Austrian duke as Lymoges, so the character Austria is this nobleman.

clue.text: Like cricket sometimes, a game which Conan Doyle wrote stories about

definitions.text: which Conan Doyle wrote stories about

parts.note: a cricket match can be long, a Test lasting five days
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Cricket and another game appear as the subject of some Sherlock Holmes creator's tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Conan Doyle published a collection called Tales of Long Ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's collection Tales of Long Ago gathers historical stories set in bygone times.

clue.text: I left men wandering around paths in the forest featured in my best-known work

definitions.text: I left men wandering around paths in the forest featured in my best-known work

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of I, L and men roam into a new order

explanation.surface: An author recalls leaving characters strolling through the woods of his most famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges I, L and MEN. Read as a whole, the clue is the author speaking of the Hundred Acre Wood in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne set Winnie-the-Pooh in the Hundred Acre Wood, where his characters roam the woodland trails.

clue.text: Late German author's wife, with boring story about a detective's wife in danger

definitions.text: about a detective's wife in danger

parts.note: the wife of the late Günter Grass is his widow, a Grass widow, with the possessive kept
a tale can be a long, tedious story

explanation.surface: A dead German novelist's widow has a dull story to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: Günter Grass, author of The Tin Drum, died in 2015. Ellis Peters's novel has Bunty Felse, the detective's wife, in peril while her husband is away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Peters's Felse novel puts Bunty, wife of the policeman George Felse, in jeopardy.

clue.text: "This is something very precious I left behind" confessed to god

indicators.note: behind means I and the left abbreviation come after the other pieces

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to a deity that they abandoned a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places I and L after SANGRA. The Sangrail is the Holy Grail of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail of Arthurian legend is the most precious of relics, sought by the knights.

clue.text: Gore hadn't troubled Zamyatin's soldier in a short story

definitions.text: Zamyatin's soldier in a short story

indicators.note: troubled means the letters of the two words before it are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former US vice-president was not bothered by a Russian writer's fictional soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges GORE and HADNT (the apostrophe adds nothing). Yevgeny Zamyatin wrote a very short story about a Red Army soldier portrayed as a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamyatin's brief tale of revolutionary Petrograd is titled after its monstrous soldier figure.

clue.text: Master in Latin with merit

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone with a master's degree in Latin who deserves praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a subject is to acquire it thoroughly, to get it by study.

clue.text: An agricultural area settled in France

definitions.meaning: open grazing land for livestock, as in the American West
the French word for settled, orderly or steady in one's ways

explanation.definitionFit: Grazing land is called a range, and the French adjective for steady or orderly is spelt the same.

clue.text: One assisting with change of lines when a farceur meets the Queen

definitions.text: One assisting with change of lines

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A writer of stage farces is introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers was the English writer of farces such as Rookery Nook; a traverser is a railway device moving carriages sideways between tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: On a railway, a traverser is a platform that shifts rolling stock from one track to a parallel one.

clue.text: He's written of the orient sheikh involved with no ladies

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: An Arab sheikh is caught up with a group that includes no women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SHEIKH and NOLADIES together; 'with' just joins them. The Afghan-American novelist wrote The Kite Runner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afghan-born novelist wrote The Kite Runner and other books set in Afghanistan, an eastern land.

clue.text: Somewhere in Wiltshire is the commonest earl in Shakespeare

definitions.meaning: a cathedral city in the English county of Wiltshire
an earl of this title appears in several of the history plays, from King John to Henry VI

explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city lies in Wiltshire, and earls of that title appear across the history plays.

clue.text: Monarch enthralled by Charlie's support, on the throne in a capital city

parts.note: the throne and the can are both slang for the toilet

indicators.note: enthralled by means the monarch is held captive inside the support

parts.note: charlies is British slang for breasts, so their support is a bra
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A king captivated by the backing of Prince Charles, newly crowned, in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the throne' looks regal, but throne is slang for the toilet. Charlies is British slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is Australia's seat of government, its federal capital.

clue.text: Rejected Elizabeth, initially embraced by everyone except one, will reportedly reject Tom she'll marry a vicar's son in the end

definitions.text: she'll marry a vicar's son in the end

indicators.note: Rejected means the whole first part is turned round and read the other way
embraced by means the letter is held inside the phrase for everyone except one

parts.note: everyone means all
except means bar, as in 'all bar one'
one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of Elizabeth is used
reportedly means the word will is taken by its sound, spelt with a single L

parts.note: the word will, heard rather than written

indicators.note: reject means the name Tom is turned round

explanation.surface: A jilted Elizabeth, half-adopted by a crowd, refuses Tom and marries the clergyman's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns round everything up to the comma, giving ARABELLA. In Goldsmith's The Vicar of Wakefield she marries George, the vicar's son.
explanation.definitionFit: In Goldsmith's novel this heiress finally weds George Primrose, eldest boy of the Wakefield clergyman.

clue.text: Influenced to accept a promise, like Uriah Heep

indicators.note: to accept means the word for influenced takes the other piece into it

parts.note: led means guided or influenced
an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Someone was persuaded to take a vow, like the Dickens villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning, scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, hated by the hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's oily clerk was detested by David Copperfield and most readers.

clue.text: Whoever primarily worked in a wheelhouse was engulfed

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of Whoever is taken

parts.note: to helm a ship is to steer it from the wheelhouse

explanation.surface: Whoever was steering the boat got swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelm is to submerge or overwhelm, as a wave does a boat.

clue.text: A playwright's story with suffering

parts.note: a story or joke is 'the one about...'
ill means suffering or unwell

explanation.surface: A dramatist's tale accompanies illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill was the American dramatist of Long Day's Journey into Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill wrote The Iceman Cometh and won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: A writer of drama, mostly gritty, died in a Cheshire town

indicators.note: mostly means the word for gritty loses its final letter

parts.note: a gritty, grim drama can be called bleak

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for died goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Sale is a town south of Manchester, historically in Cheshire

explanation.surface: A grim dramatist passed away in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BLEAK to BLEA. Sale is a town in the north-west of England, traditionally in Cheshire. Alan Bleasdale wrote Boys from the Blackstuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bleasdale is the Liverpool television playwright behind Boys from the Blackstuff and GBH.

clue.text: In one book he wrote about smoking ovens — revolutionary volume for many?

definitions.text: In one book he wrote about smoking

indicators.note: revolutionary means the altered word turns round and is read backwards
for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: N stands for an indefinite large number

explanation.surface: An author's book about smoking kilns, a radical tome for the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: In ovens 'volume for many' puts V for N, giving OVEVS, which 'revolutionary' turns round. Italo Svevo's Zeno's Conscience follows a man trying to give up smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Italo Svevo's novel Zeno's Conscience follows a narrator endlessly vowing to quit cigarettes.

clue.text: American in a hospital in Hampshire, in drama

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for American sits inside the word for hospital

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: An American patient in a hospital in the English county of Hampshire, staged as a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire looks like the English county, but it is the actress Susan Hampshire, known for TV drama such as The Forsyte Saga.
explanation.definitionFit: The English actress of The Forsyte Saga, surnamed Hampshire, has this as her first name.

clue.text: Right way to cultivate a flower in France

parts.note: to hone a skill is to cultivate or refine it

explanation.surface: Advice on the proper method for growing a French bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is a crossword's river, something that flows; the Rhône runs through France.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a thing that flows, a river, and this one crosses south-eastern France.

clue.text: Famous user of code is a radio operator knocking back strong drink, albeit oddly

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator

indicators.note: knocking back suggests the word for strong drink is turned the other way

parts.note: rum is a strong spirit

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of albeit

explanation.surface: A radio amateur is downing spirits, though in a strange manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' gives MUR, and 'oddly' picks ABI from albeit. Hammurabi was the Babylonian king famous for his code of laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The Babylonian king issued one of the earliest written law codes, carved on a basalt stele.

clue.text: Cad beaten up going around New York is the victim in a classic mystery

definitions.text: the victim in a classic mystery

indicators.note: going around means the scrambled cad surrounds the other piece
beaten up means the letters of Cad are knocked into a new order
New means the letters of York are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gets a beating on a trip round New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' makes ACD from Cad and 'New' makes KROY from York; 'going around' puts KROY inside ACD. Roger Ackroyd is the murder victim in Agatha Christie's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's The Murder of Roger Ackroyd centres on the killing of this squire.

clue.text: Unknown group on road heading west, that could be AA

indicators.note: on means the reversed road piece comes first, with the rest placed on it
heading west in an across clue means the road abbreviation is written right to left

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown
a cell is a small group, as of activists

explanation.surface: A mystery band travelling down the road towards the west, which might be the motoring organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' turns RD into DR. AA looks like the Automobile Association, a British breakdown service, but here it is a battery size.
explanation.definitionFit: An AA is a standard size of battery, and such a battery holds its electrolyte as a paste.
